claims.text: Surface mechanical attrition treatment can create a gradient nanostructured surface layer in a coarse-grained metal.
A SMAT-induced gradient nanostructure can concurrently improve strength and ductility.
SMAT creates ultrafine-grained surface regions over a coarse-grained core.
The resulting structure has a hard ultrafine-grained surface that transitions into a softer coarse-grained interior.
Ultrafine surface grains act as dislocation barriers.
Dislocation blocking by the ultrafine surface grains enhances strength.
The coarse-grained core retains ductility by permitting more effective plastic deformation.
The gradient structure produces a synergistic mechanical interaction between the surface and core during deformation.
SMAT-treated metal will have higher yield strength than an untreated coarse-grained counterpart.
SMAT-treated metal will have higher ultimate tensile strength than an untreated coarse-grained counterpart.
SMAT-treated metal will have improved ductility relative to an untreated coarse-grained counterpart.
The approach is expected to be effective for thin to moderately thick metallic components in which a pronounced gradient can be established.
The effectiveness of the approach may be limited in very thick bulk materials.
